acca.note: An assessed programme, listed by name for Kaplan Singapore and authorised for graduates to 31 December 2030. A graduate who passed those units holds up to 9 of the 13 (the FAQ’s ceiling: “A maximum of nine Applied Knowledge and Applied Skills exams of the ACCA Qualification can be awarded.”).

notes: All three tools were read on 2026-10-26 in a browser, as a visitor uses them: ACCA’s Exemptions calculator (institution › graduation year 2026 › course, or “Can't find your course?” › qualification type › subject category), CPA Australia’s accredited course search (country › provider › year), and CFA Institute’s affiliated-university search (by name). No login, challenge or disallowed path was involved.

The 13 ACCA exams are the nine Applied Knowledge and Applied Skills exams, the two Essentials and two of the four Options. ACCA’s exemptions FAQ (https://www.accaglobal.com/gb/en/help/exemptions.html): “A maximum of nine Applied Knowledge and Applied Skills exams of the ACCA Qualification can be awarded.” “For example, a student who has completed a programme which has not been assessed by ACCA may be awarded up to a maximum of the first four exams of the ACCA Qualification.”

For a degree ACCA has not assessed, the calculator offers the national-qualification list of the awarding university’s country (Ireland, the United Kingdom or Australia here). The same FAQ says: “If your qualification has not been assessed and does not appear on the list of national qualifications for the country where you studied, no exemptions will be awarded.” Kaplan’s students study in Singapore; ACCA settles which list applies when it assesses the application.

Which subject category an unassessed degree falls in is Kaplan 360++’s rule: the degree title matched against the subject-title examples ACCA shows for each category (General Business & Management, Accounting Major, Accounting Joint/Minor, Finance, Law). ACCA marks each list “Please note this list is not definitive.” The outcomes per category are the same in Ireland, the United Kingdom and Australia: General Business & Management BT; Accounting Major BT, MA, FA, LW; Accounting Joint/Minor and Finance BT, MA, FA; Law LW; Non-relevant none. A business degree with law as a joint or minor subject adds LW.

ACCA’s FAQ: “What is a conditional exemption? ACCA offers conditional exemptions to students who are studying an assessed course and will graduate at a date in the future.” The two assessed Kaplan programmes (Murdoch accounting, Portsmouth accountancy and financial management) offer them.

ACCA is redesigning the qualification (https://www.accaglobal.com/gb/en/help/future-qualification.html): “In July 2027, all exemptions against the current qualification will be automatically transitioned over to the redesigned qualification in line with our published transition rules, and displayed on the Exemptions Calculator.” “Up until June 2027, all applications will be assessed against the current qualification.” The counts here are against the current 13 exams.

CPA Australia’s search page: “By completing accredited courses and the subjects specified for each course, you will maximise your entry point into the CPA Program. But don't panic if your program is not listed. When you apply for membership all qualifications are considered.” A degree marked not-listed is assessed on application.

CFA Institute affiliates named degree programmes at a university, wherever they are taught; no Kaplan degree is among them. University College Dublin (MSc in Finance), Birmingham City University (BSc in Finance and Investment) and Monash University (finance and banking degrees) are affiliated for other programmes; Murdoch, Northumbria, Portsmouth and Kaplan return no result.

ISCA’s Singapore CA Qualification (SCAQ), read on 2026-10-26 on isca.org.sg: the Professional Programme page (academic requirements), the Foundation Programme page (accredited degrees, module exemption guides) and the list of recognised universities (“Updated as of Mar 2026”). Professional Programme page: “Applicants need to have one of the following: 1. Direct Entry Degree … 2. Accredited Degree or Other degrees”. The direct entry degrees are accountancy degrees of NTU, NUS, SMU, SUSS and SIT; no Kaplan degree is one. Accredited means the degree is named on ISCA’s accredited-degree list; recognised means the awarding university is on the recognised-universities list; not-listed means neither. The qualification ends in the CA (Singapore) title: “Apply to be a CA (Singapore).”

CPA Ireland: every “Become A Student” page on cpaireland.ie (Exemptions, Still in College, Entry Routes) redirects to the amalgamation page, read on 2026-10-26: “CPA Ireland is no longer accepting new student registrations.” Its exemptions checker for UCD degrees is no longer reachable.

Chartered Accountants Ireland replaces CPA Ireland for University College Dublin degrees: CPA Ireland’s page says “CPA Ireland is no longer accepting new student registrations.”, and Chartered Accountants Ireland’s about-us page (https://www.charteredaccountants.ie/about-us, read 2026-10-26) says “On 1 September 2024, members and students of CPA Ireland became incorporated into Chartered Accountants to create the largest professional body on the island of Ireland.” Its exemptions list and entry-route pages were read on 2026-10-26.
